title: Adaptive Intake Funnel for Console Analytics Requests with SLA Tiering
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers submit a large volume of ad-hoc console/reporting requests (usage exports, tenant cost breakdowns, custom dashboard builds). Triage today is manual and inconsistent: tickets are often missing key signals, delivery estimates vary widely, and high-cost requests slip SLA windows. That causes frustration for Sales/Support and increases PM/Eng churn.

Goal: Build an adaptive intake funnel that reduces manual triage, shortens time-to-first-response, and routes requests into clear SLA lanes (Self-serve, Standard <14d, Priority <5d). The funnel should automate signal enrichment, provide upfront cost/effort estimates, and generate routing metadata that can be consumed by engineering and concierge teams.

Proposed solution:
1) New intake form in Console with progressive disclosure: minimal fields for self-serve requests and expanded fields for enterprise lanes (data volume, retention window, export cadence, required columns, primary tenant examples, downstream consumers).
2) Automated enrichment microservice: when form submitted, the service queries telemetry to attach footprint estimates (avg daily tokens, embedding units, model variants used), flags for PII/regulated data (based on existing classification hooks), and suggests a template (CSV export, scheduled daily, dashboard slice).
3) Routing & SLA engine: evaluate inputs + enrichment to assign request to lanes: SELF_SERVE, STANDARD, PRIORITY. Each lane has SLOs and allowed resource bundles. Priority lane requires customer sponsor & business justification.
4) Cost & effort estimator: rule-based heuristic that turns signals into a 3-point effort estimate (small/medium/large) and a rough cost run-rate. Display estimate to customer and add to ticket metadata.
5) Admin console for triage owners: queue with filtering by lane, tenant size, estimated effort, and SLA countdown. Integrations: Support (Zendesk), Sales (Salesforce link), and a GitHub template for engineering work items.

Acceptance criteria:
- Intake form implemented with required fields per lane and validations.
- Enrichment service returns footprint estimates and PII/regulation flags >= 90% of submissions in pilot.
- Routing engine assigns a lane automatically >= 85% of pilot requests with manual override.
- Cost/effort estimator present and surfaced to requestor before submission.
- Admin triage UI with filters and SLA timers; exportable queue to CSV.
- Pilot with 3 enterprise customers (Finance, AdTech, Healthcare) and SLA met for 90% of Priority lane tickets during pilot.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Friction vs signal: requiring too many fields will push requests to Support; too few and routing accuracy drops. We'll start with minimal required fields and progressive disclosure.
- Data sensitivity: enrichment requires telemetry access; must respect KMS/HSM policies for PII flags and ensure no raw customer payloads are stored.
- Accuracy of cost estimator: this will be heuristic initially; we’ll instrument and iterate based on actual delivery telemetry.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: lightweight form UX + validation + spec review (Design + Eng).
- Week 2-3: build enrichment microservice and routing prototype; internal QA with sample tickets.
- Week 4: admin triage UI and integrations (Zendesk, Salesforce link).
- Week 5: run 2-week pilot with 3 customers, collect metrics, adjust routing rules.
- Post-pilot: general availability in console and playbook for sales/support.
